_comment: Qwen3.5/3.6 multi-token-prediction head. It ships inside its target's HF checkpoint, so its configs are the target's verbatim HF config (which declares `mtp_num_hidden_layers`) and it registers under the identity `qwen3_5_mtp` — the `model_type` MLX gives the head's separate drafter repo (named from the target's: `org/X-4bit` → `org/X-MTP-4bit`, `drafter_repo_infix`), whose tensors are stored bare (`fc.*`, `layers.0.*`, `norm.*`, `pre_fc_norm_*`; hence the empty decoder prefix). It has no embed_tokens / lm_head of its own: the loader lends it the target's. Its decoder layers are the MTP layers, so `num_hidden_layers` REPLACES the backbone's count with `mtp_num_hidden_layers`. Norms as the Qwen3.5 family (zero-centered on HF checkpoints; MLX-affine ones store the full gain, which the norm offset rule reads as-is); the routed experts renormalize top-k as the target's. It DRAFTS OVER A VOCABULARY PREFIX: its logits are the target lm_head's first 65536 rows (`vocab_size`; token ids in BPE merge order, the most frequent first), so a draft costs a quarter of the 248k-row lm_head read; it embeds every token (`embed_vocab_size`). Every emitted token is still the target's choice (a draft is only a proposal it verifies); what the prefix costs is the drafts it cannot make: on the MLX oracle (k=3, code/story/repeat prompts) 2.85 tokens per verify step against 2.94 at the full vocabulary. Halving again does not pay: at k=2 on the bench prompts (the same oracle) 32768 costs 3.9% tokens a step against 65536 — the head's full-vocabulary top-1 leaves the half prefix on about 13% of positions — several times the ~1-2% of a verify cycle the halved lm_head read saves, while 65536 costs 1.5% against the full vocabulary, well under what its 4x smaller read saves. It drafts `spec_drafts` tokens a step while the step holds at most `spec_max_seqs` sequences: two — a verify step of two runs six rows, within the eight-row verify-sized bucket (`pick_bucket`: the smallest `bucket_m` at or past the rows), amortizing the step's fixed cost — and one request pays on both GPUs measured (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, with drafts vs without: base M5 output tok/s 1.36-1.38x sampled; M5 Max, at this head, TPOT 1.33x on the code prompt and 1.51x on a long one, greedy). Past the gate the head's pass 1 still runs, KV-only (no lm_head, no drafts), so its requests keep their head KV and draft again once the step is back within the gate. Above two the gate waits on the verify-sized rungs: a verify step of three runs nine rows, past the eight-row bucket onto the 64-row prefill-shaped tape, and where a larger gate pays depends on the GPU and on the target (a dense one's rows cost far less). TODO: one gate per device profile and target, derived at expansion from the verify and plain tapes' costs (scratchy_serving_engine::spec_decode::mtp's module docs carry the measurements, with the rest of MTP's open work). Its KV is its target's capacity (a pool mirroring the target's blocks), so its KV codec is decided at the target's layer count (`target_num_hidden_layers`, its config's `num_hidden_layers`): the target's codec, under which it stages through the target's scratch.
